newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end up a hair on inflation data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end up a hair on inflation data.

text.p: Mexican stocks fended off a bout of profit-taking and edged higher Monday after a government report showed inflation was a shade lower than had been expected.
"The inflation figures were good, better than expected. I think that's what propped stocks up at the close," said Roberto Galvan, an analyst with the Bursametrica consultancy.
The blue chip IPC index rose 2.23 points to 3,335.12. Volume was thin at 48.4 million shares traded.
Banco de Mexico said consumer inflation in November was 1.52 percent, compared to an average forecast of 1.56 percent in a Reuters survey.
"Some buyers stepped in towards the close and that turned us around," said a trader, referring to a mid-session dip on profit-taking.
A total of 98 stocks were traded, of which losers beat gainers, 38 to 35.
Traders said the gainers list was dominated by stocks that were not typical of any particular market trend.
"Nothing special happened with any stock," a trader said.
Iusacel headed the losers, down two pesos ($0.25) to 4.98 ($0.62), after what dealers called an atypical large trade.
